scenarios.title: The Teammate's Party
scenarios.text: A teammate's party the night before an early workday, and the whole rookie class is going.

choices.label: Go for an hour
choices.result: You show up, say hello to everyone and leave before ten. Two rookies call you boring. You're the only one awake in the morning meeting.

choices.label: Stay home
choices.result: You stay home and get nine hours of sleep. You hear the stories at breakfast and feel fine about missing them.

choices.label: Stay until the end
choices.result: You stay until three. The workday is a blur, and {coach} asks if you're sick.

scenarios.title: The New City
scenarios.text: You can explore {town} or stay in your apartment with the blinds closed.

choices.label: Explore one neighborhood a week
choices.result: You pick a neighborhood every week and walk it. By midseason you know {town} better than some teammates who grew up here.

choices.label: Find one place to belong
choices.result: You find one diner, one gym and one coffee shop and become a regular at all three.

choices.label: Stay in
choices.result: You stay in your apartment between practices. It's restful, and {town} stays a stranger.

scenarios.title: The Family Visit
scenarios.text: {parent} and {sibling} want to visit for a weekend, and your schedule doesn't have a weekend in it.

choices.label: Make it work
choices.result: You give them the guest room, practice in the morning and spend every evening with them. You're exhausted and happy.

choices.label: Ask them to come in the offseason
choices.result: You ask them to wait for the offseason. {parent} understands; {sibling} is disappointed.

choices.label: Bring them to practice
choices.result: You get them passes to a practice and lunch with the team. {sibling} talks about it for months.

scenarios.title: The Unexpected Attention
scenarios.text: Someone recognizes you at the grocery store and follows you down three aisles, talking the whole time.

choices.label: Be gracious
choices.result: You stop, talk and take a photo. It costs you ten minutes and makes someone's week.

choices.label: Keep moving, politely
choices.result: You smile, say thanks and keep moving. They post that you were 'a little cold'.

choices.label: Shop at night
choices.result: You start shopping at eleven at night. Nobody recognizes you, and the cereal aisle is all yours.

scenarios.title: The Local Radio Appearance
scenarios.text: A sports radio show invites you on, live, during drive time.

choices.label: Prepare and go
choices.result: You prepare three stories and keep it light. The host invites you back.

choices.label: Wing it
choices.result: You go on without notes. One joke lands; one answer about the coaching staff gets replayed all week.

choices.label: Decline
choices.result: You decline politely and spend the hour at the net.

scenarios.title: The Practice Routine
scenarios.text: Your college routine isn't working at this level, and you need a new one by Sunday.

choices.label: Copy the veteran's routine
choices.result: You copy the veteran snapper's pre-kick routine step for step. It feels strange, then it feels like yours.

choices.label: Build your own
choices.result: You build your own routine from scratch, charting every kick for a week.

choices.label: Ask {coach}
choices.result: You ask {coach} to help you build it. The coach is pleased you asked.

scenarios.title: The First Contract Question
scenarios.text: A reporter asks whether you expect an extension, and you haven't kicked a regular-season game yet.

choices.label: Laugh it off
choices.result: You laugh and say you're just trying to keep your locker. The quote is charming, and nobody reads into it.

choices.label: Say you've earned a look
choices.result: You say you think you've earned a look. The front office reads it, and so does the veteran kicker.

choices.label: Decline to answer
choices.result: You say contracts are your agent's job. It's dull and smart.

scenarios.title: The Teammate's Struggle
scenarios.text: A fellow rookie is falling apart: late to meetings, quiet at lunch, gone the minute practice ends.

choices.label: Check on him
choices.result: You knock on his door after practice and stay for an hour. He doesn't say much, but he shows up early the next day.

choices.label: Tell a veteran
choices.result: You quietly tell a veteran you trust. The veteran handles it better than you could have.

choices.label: Mind your own business
choices.result: You've got your own roster spot to worry about. He's released a month later, and you think about it longer than you expected.

scenarios.title: The Family Expectations
scenarios.text: Your family expects more now that you're earning, and they're not shy about it.

choices.label: Set a family budget
choices.result: You sit down with {parent} and set a yearly amount for family help. It's awkward and it ends the guessing.

choices.label: Say yes to everything
choices.result: You say yes to every request. It feels good, and your account feels it more.

choices.label: Say not yet
choices.result: You explain that a rookie contract isn't forever money. Some of them understand.

scenarios.title: The Unexpected Bill
scenarios.text: Your car's transmission dies the week before a road trip, and the repair costs more than the car is worth.

choices.label: Fix it
choices.result: You pay for the repair and take the bus to practice for a week. The veterans think it's hilarious.

choices.label: Buy something new
choices.result: You buy a new car the same day. It's lovely, and the payment is going to follow you around for years.

choices.label: Ask a teammate for rides
choices.result: You ask a teammate for rides until you figure it out. You become friends on those drives.

scenarios.title: The Former Coach Calls
scenarios.text: Your old college coach calls to check in, and asks how you're really doing.

choices.label: Tell the truth
choices.result: You tell the truth: it's harder than you expected. The coach tells you about every player who said the same thing and made it.

choices.label: Say everything's great
choices.result: You say everything's great. The coach doesn't believe you and says so, kindly.

choices.label: Ask for help
choices.result: You ask for help with one specific problem. The coach watches your film and calls back the next day.

scenarios.title: The Community Invitation
scenarios.text: A local school asks you to speak to its athletes about what it takes.

choices.label: Speak honestly
choices.result: You tell them about the cuts, the doubts and the practice you nearly quit. Three kids stay after to ask questions.

choices.label: Run a kicking clinic instead
choices.result: You skip the speech and run a kicking clinic on their field. Everyone gets muddy.

choices.label: Decline politely
choices.result: You decline because of the schedule. They invite someone else.

scenarios.title: The Dating Question
scenarios.text: Someone you meet at a teammate's dinner seems more interested in the league than in you.

choices.label: Ask them out anyway
choices.result: You ask them out. They ask a lot about the league, and a little about you. You don't call again, and you learn to spot it faster.

choices.label: Change the subject
choices.result: You keep steering the conversation away from football. By dessert, they're laughing at your terrible cooking stories.

choices.label: Leave early
choices.result: You thank the host and leave early. You'd rather be bored than be a résumé.
